division: S. W. Sherman (signed at the head, where the printed page number stands on this group's other left sheets)
read_pass: the recapitulation leaf read in full (T-0966, piece 4 of T-0746)
printed_page_note: no printed page number is legible where this form carries it; the top-right corner carries the marshal's signature and nothing else. It is not guessed from the run of its neighbours (T-0741).
page_kind_note: NOT AN ENUMERATING PAGE, and no household, person or serial may be hung on any line of it. The left-sheet form is used as a RECAPITULATION of the Chicago city enumeration: the NAMES OF HEADS OF FAMILIES column carries the numbers 1 to 30 under a written heading 'Page', each numbered page carries its own totals across the free-white age bands and the free-coloured columns, and a brace in the left margin gathers the thirty pages into First through Sixth Ward. The margin heading reads 'Recapitulation of [?] (Chicago City) preceding pages', one word struck through before the parenthesis.
lines_note: thirty numbered lines, 1 to 30, plus five written ward-subtotal rows and one grand-total row. The Fourth Ward is a single page and is closed by a rule with no subtotal row of its own.
cells_note: every free-white male and female age-band cell and every free-coloured cell of all thirty lines is read off the deposited page image at 2x to 5x with the column rules of this leaf drawn over the crop, so that a figure's column is measured rather than judged by eye. A cell with no mark is 0, which on a recapitulation is a reading and not an absence: the enumerator ruled the whole table and left the unused bands empty on every line. Nothing beyond the 70-80 male band and the 70-80 female band carries a mark anywhere on the leaf.

column_geometry.derived_by: vertical printed rules measured on this leaf over y 560-2990 at a 0.35-0.50 continuity threshold, then fitted: the free-white male block is 13 columns of 80.4 px between 793 and 1838, the free-white female block 13 columns of 80.8 px between 1838 and 2888, the free-coloured block 12 columns of 81.3 px between 2888 and 3862
column_geometry.note: the three right-most free-coloured candidates the sweep returns (3690, 3754, 3807) are NOT the last three rules: they do not fit the block's own pitch and they sit where the leaf curls into the binding. The block is fitted from its measured MALES/FEMALES divider at 3376, which is exactly six columns of 81.3 px from 2888. No entry on this leaf stands right of 3619, so nothing in the reading depends on that fit.

ward_rules_px.derived_by: full-width horizontal rules found on a darkness profile of the free-white female block, which carries the least pen ink
ward_rules_px.note: each ward subtotal is written INSIDE a pair of rules 24 to 37 px apart and the rules cross its glyphs. That is why five of the six subtotal rows are harder to read than the thirty lines above them, and why the lines are treated as senior to the subtotal wherever they disagree.

ward_note: 8, 9, 2, 1, 3 and 7 pages. The brace and its written ward names are the evidence; the closing rules are where each brace ends.

blocks.why_no_subtotal: the ward is ONE enumerating page, so the enumerator closed it with a rule and wrote no separate subtotal row: page 20's own line IS the ward total. Printed 237's fourth block is likewise a single line standing between two rules with no footing of its own (33S7-9YYJ-V2, block 4, 189).

grand_total.note: the free-white MALE half of the grand total is the strongest single check on this reading: read cell by cell it sums to 2407 and the enumerator's own grand-total row sums to 2407 as well, with the per-column differences cancelling exactly. The free-white female half does not do that - 2026 read against 2019 written - and the seven persons are left open.
grand_total.persons_written_in_the_grand_total_row_n: 4,475 is the sum of the grand-total row AS READ: 2,407 free white males, 2,019 free white females and 49 free coloured persons. The free-coloured 10-to-24 female cell of that row carries no legible mark while the ward subtotals above it hold 4 there, so the free-coloured half of the row is 49 read against 53 summed. That cell is recorded null, not 0 and not 4.

against_printed_237.what_this_is: printed 237 (33S7-9YYJ-V2, read by T-0529) is the OTHER recapitulation the enumeration book's certificate page names. It carries thirty ruled lines of division totals gathered into six blocks. This leaf carries thirty numbered pages gathered into six WARDS. The two are compared here line for line for the first time.
against_printed_237.block_shape: 237's six blocks hold 8, 9, 2, 1, 3 and 7 lines. This leaf's six wards hold 8, 9, 2, 1, 3 and 7 pages. The shapes are identical, in order, including the two that are unlike anything else on either sheet: 237's fourth block is a LONE LINE of 189 with no footing, and the Fourth Ward here is a LONE PAGE closed by a rule with no subtotal; 237's fifth block is the three lines its own footing is illegible over, and the Fifth Ward here is three pages.
against_printed_237.what_that_settles: printed 237's six blocks ARE the six wards of the city of Chicago, and its thirty division totals are the thirty enumerating pages in order. 237 could not say so; it carries no ward name. This is the first attribution of any 1840 Chicago enumerating page to a ward.
against_printed_237.agreement: 19 of 30 pages agree to the person between two independently written leaves.
against_printed_237.where_they_do_not: the eleven that differ are named in line_by_line with their signed difference. Nine of the eleven are within 6 persons. Two are not: page 1 stands 11 over 237 and page 24 stands 19 over it. Page 24's line is the one this leaf writes hard against the Sixth Ward's opening rule, which crosses its upper halves; page 1's is clear, and its excess is unexplained.
against_printed_237.totals: the thirty lines read here sum to 4,486 persons. 237's thirty division totals sum to 4,466, and 4,470 is written at 237's foot and at the book's certificate page. Neither leaf is adjusted to meet the other.

why_no_serial_can_hang_on_any_line: every line of this leaf is a PAGE of the enumeration, not a household. It names nobody. No IPUMS serial, no resident and no household may be derived from it; what it carries is a ward attribution for each enumerating page and a population for each.
records_note: one record per numbered page of the enumeration, 1 to 30, in the enumerator's own order. 'as_read' is the figure written in the first column, which on this leaf is a page number and not a name.
